body: We must be very explicit about which exceptions will get there. For example: Should an extension context see exceptions that occurred in other extension points and in other implementations of the same extension point? Or just from the same extension? Or just from the current test?

Good questions!

The `testException` should in fact be an exception thrown during invocation of the test method. If we don't have clarity in this regard it would then be difficult if not impossible for an extension to properly react to such an exception. For example, if a developer wants to implement his own version of `@ExpectedException` using the JUnit 5 extension model, such an extension would need to access exactly the exception thrown from the test method and not from some other extension.

I tend to think that an exception thrown from a `@BeforeEach` or `@AfterEach` method should also be considered as a `testException`.

Regarding exceptions thrown by extensions, we could consider introducing an `extensionException` for that dedicated purpose. Clients of `TestExtensionContext` would then have to decide which of the two exceptions they need to support.

I think we should also consider introducing similar support for `ContainerExtensionContext`.

Thoughts?

Idea: Let's introduce a new extension point à la

interface ExcpetionThrownInTest extends ExtensionPoint {
   void exceptionThrown(TestExtensionContext context, Throwable throwable);
}

The callback would be invoked for all exceptions except AssertionError. Impementors could swallow or rethrow the exception.

Advantages:
- An extension can deal with exceptions in one place and not in all implemented extension points
- ExtensionContext need not be changed.

That unfortunately won't meet all of our needs.

Extensions that _wrap_ the test invocation with a _before_/_after_ callback pair need access to the exception in the _after_ callback.

For example, if a `DatabaseTransactionExtension` starts a transaction in the _before_ callback, it will either need to commit or roll back the transaction in the _after_ callback. In such cases, rollback behavior is typically influenced by the type of exception thrown.

In other words, _after_ callbacks will often need to process a test exception alongside the standard _after_ logic: separating _after_ logic and _exception handling_ logic into two different methods within an extension leads to cumbersome implementations at best.

Well, the exceptionThrown EP can store it as attribute for other EPs to pick up if need be.

Sure, it _could_, but... I don't see any need to make extension developers jump through hoops just to access the exception.

Accessing the exception should be just as easy as accessing the test class, instance, or method.

repository.name: junit-framework
repository.description: ✅ The programmer-friendly testing framework for Java and the JVM

issue.body:
## Status Quo

In contrast to the behavior of JUnit 4, the Jupiter `TestEngine` currently does not invoke any "after each" methods or callbacks if an exception is thrown during test execution or by a "before each" method or callback.
## Related Issues
- #92
- #359 
## Deliverables
- [x] Ensure that "after each" methods and callbacks are invoked even if an exception is thrown by the test method or a "before each" method or callback.

issue.body:
## Status Quo

In contrast to the behavior of JUnit 4, the Jupiter `TestEngine` currently does not invoke `AfterAllCallback`s or `@AfterAll` methods if an exception is thrown by a `BeforeAllCallback` or `@BeforeAll` method.

## Related Issues

- #92
- #357

## Deliverables

- [x] Ensure that "after all" methods and callbacks are invoked even if an exception is thrown by a "before all" method or callback.

issue.title: Introduce support for JUnit 5 in the TestContext framework [SPR-13575]
issue.body:
**[Juergen Hoeller](https://jira.spring.io/secure/ViewProfile.jspa?name=juergen.hoeller)** opened **[SPR-13575](https://jira.spring.io/browse/SPR-13575?redirect=false)** and commented

#### Work in Progress

The current work for supporting JUnit 5 in the _Spring TestContext Framework_ can be seen in the [spring-test-junit5](https://github.com/sbrannen/spring-test-junit5) repository.

#### Feedback is Welcome

Developers are encouraged to try out the `SpringExtension` and provide feedback!

#### Deliverables

1. [x] Introduce a `SpringExtension` to be configured via `@ExtendWith(SpringExtension.class)` (analogous to `@RunWith(SpringRunner.class)` for JUnit 4)
2. [x] Implement `ParameterResolver`
3. [x] Implement `BeforeAllCallback`
4. [x] Implement `AfterAllCallback`
5. [x] Implement `TestInstancePostProcessor`
6. [x] Implement `BeforeEachCallback`
7. [x] Implement `AfterEachCallback`
8. [x] Implement `BeforeTestExecutionCallback` and `AfterTestExecutionCallback`
   - [x] depends on #9043
9. [x] Delete custom `MethodParameterFactory`
   - [x] depends on #18627
10. [x] Migrate to `ExecutionContext.Store`
    - [x] Depends on [JUnit issue #347](https://github.com/junit-team/junit5/issues/347)
    - [x] Depends on [JUnit issue #349](https://github.com/junit-team/junit5/issues/349)
11. [x] Provide the test exception to `TestContextManager.afterTestMethod()`
    - [x] depends on [JUnit issue #92](https://github.com/junit-team/junit5/issues/92), [JUnit issue #357](https://github.com/junit-team/junit5/issues/357), [JUnit issue #359](https://github.com/junit-team/junit5/issues/359)
